clue.text: Break for two engineers on the ship

parts.note: RE (Royal Engineers, a British army corps) and CE (civil engineer) are two kinds of engineer
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Two engineers on board a vessel are given time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two engineers' supplies two different abbreviations, RE (Royal Engineers) and CE (civil engineer), and 'on the ship' tacks SS on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or interval, as when Parliament or a court stops sitting.

clue.text: Geoff sat out in the wings

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Geoff sat waiting off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors waiting in the wings are beside the stage, out of the audience's view.

clue.text: The way we read of a Tory gain

definitions.meaning: English text runs across the page starting at one side
when a Conservative wins a seat, it passes from a left-wing party to a right-wing one

explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: English is read in that direction, and a Conservative gain shifts a seat politically in the same direction, from Labour's side to the Tories'.

clue.text: Miserable one abroad, a dwarf

parts.note: un is French for one
Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A lonely foreigner is a wretched little fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy and miserable are synonyms for feeling sad.

clue.text: Cavalier-like sailor takes a ship to seek out a kookaburra

parts.note: The Laughing Cavalier is a famous portrait by Frans Hals
Jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: A dashing seaman boards a vessel to hunt down an Australian bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier-like' points to the Frans Hals painting The Laughing Cavalier, so it gives LAUGHING; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old Australian name for the kookaburra, a bird famous for its cackling call.

clue.text: Measure nothing more than the size of paper

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid, two pints
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A measurement that is no bigger than a sheet's dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than' is a link: the measure comes first and nothing follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarto is a book or paper format made by folding a sheet twice into four leaves.

clue.text: Heads or tails it remains the same

indicators.note: says the word is unchanged when read backwards, the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way the coin lands, nothing changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads or tails' suggests a coin, and the word reads the same both ways. The anna was an old Indian coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin has a heads side and a tails side, and the anna was a former coin of India.

clue.text: Performing flea, one of many on a tree

definitions.text: one of many on a tree

indicators.note: a performing flea does tricks, so the letters go through a routine and rearrange

explanation.surface: A circus flea, one of many perched in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree carries a great many leaves on its branches.

clue.text: I leave the wreck and flee

indicators.note: I leave means the letter I departs from the word for the wreck

parts.note: a ruin is a wreck

explanation.surface: I abandon the wrecked ship and escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away is to flee.

clue.text: Pupils of the past

parts.note: former students of a school or college, described as pupils from earlier days

explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students, graduates of an institution.

clue.text: Goods thrown out of aircraft by morning

parts.note: jets are aircraft

explanation.surface: Cargo is dumped from planes early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link putting one piece beside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship, which may wash ashore.

clue.text: African experienced rough gale and rain storm

indicators.note: storm signals the combined letters being whipped up into a new order
rough suggests the gale's letters are roughed up and jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveller came through a fierce gale and rainstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experienced' is a link; 'rough' jumbles GALE, and 'storm' then stirs those letters together with RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algerian comes from Algeria, a country in North Africa.

clue.text: One who gets out before his time

definitions.text: One who gets out before his time

parts.words: One who gets out before his time
parts.note: reads like someone leaving early, but time here is a jail sentence and getting out is breaking out

explanation.definitionFit: A jailbreaker leaves prison before completing the sentence.

clue.text: Take food although some of it repeats

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word repeats are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Eating, even though some dishes come back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating means consuming a meal, putting nourishment into the mouth.

clue.text: Sovereign produces joke within 31 days

indicators.note: within tells us the joke goes inside the month

parts.note: May is a month with 31 days
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: The monarch makes a joke during the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link. Several months have 31 days; May is the one that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is the title used for a king or queen, as in Your Majesty.

clue.text: Turkish commander right away from an Indian city

indicators.note: away from means the letter for right is taken out of the city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer leaves an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Disturb a soldier by the gallery

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Upset an infantryman standing beside the museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; the Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or unsettle, synonymous with disturb.

clue.text: Speculator is hotter revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler is a hotter radical.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist speculates, forming ideas about how things work.

clue.text: Not a squeal by companion at sound of walking in mud

indicators.note: Not a means the letter A is dropped from squeal

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: No shriek beside a friend as they trudge through the mire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. Companion of Honour is a British award, abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is the sucking, wet noise boots make in mud.

clue.text: Unchanged at the start again

parts.note: describes having made no progress and needing to begin over

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having to start afresh after getting nowhere.

clue.text: One half-day in knock-out Japanese robe

indicators.note: in tells us one and half-day sit inside the knockout

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
I is the Roman numeral one
Mon is the first half of Monday, and its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A single morning spent stunned, wearing a Japanese gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-day' is the first half of the word Monday, not twelve hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The kimono is a traditional long Japanese garment with wide sleeves.

clue.text: It is clear the French will provoke

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit after deductions
le is French for the

explanation.surface: It is obvious the French will cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate or annoy them, like a stinging plant.

clue.text: Track from the terminal

indicators.note: from means the letters are made out of terminal, reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: Railway lines leading away from the station.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramlines are the rails a tram runs on, its track.

clue.text: Bread round

definitions.meaning: something ... up into a cylinder, or a turn of a drum

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a small bread loaf, and a roll can mean a round, as of drums or a cylinder.

clue.text: Possibly take artilleryman into unarmed combat

indicators.note: into tells us the gunner goes inside the rearranged letters
possibly suggests the letters of take might be arranged another way

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner

explanation.surface: Perhaps bring a gunner into fighting without weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' looks like a hedge on the surface but signals the rearrangement; 'into' places the gunner inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art using hands and feet rather than weapons.

clue.text: Embrace large number left in church

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: A hug from a crowd on the left side of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives its own letters here; it is not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinch is a close hold, as boxers or lovers grip each other.

clue.text: Reduced price of a lettuce

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A discount on a head of salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, also called romaine.

clue.text: Sailor found in the cellar?

definitions.meaning: the cellar here is a table container for seasoning, not a basement

explanation.definitionFit: An old seaman is called a salt, and a salt cellar holds table seasoning.
